q1_speaker.title: The Broken Speaker

obj.alex: Talk to Alex on the promenade
obj.cables: Find the aux cables the seagulls stole

offer: Achi! Achi, come here. You hear that hum? My speaker is humming. Forty speakers in the car, and the one I love is humming.
And the guy with the headphones over there keeps giving me looks. Like I'm the problem. Me! I'm a gift to this beach.
Have you tried... turning it down?
Down? There is no down. Go talk to him. Tell him it's not me. It's the hum.
alex: Oh, hi. I'm doing a silent disco. It's silent. That's the whole point. That man is the opposite of the point.
Also my headphones started humming too, which is honestly offensive. They're bamboo.
His speaker hums too. Maybe it's not him. Maybe it's not you.
...Fine. The seagulls stole my aux cables anyway. Three of them. If you find them, I'll plug into his speaker. Ironically.
cables: The last cable is still warm. A seagull glares at you like you broke a contract.
outro: Okay. I plugged in. His playlist is... a lot.
His is all whales singing. Whales! Who dances to whales?
Everybody on this beach is dancing to the whales right now, Moshiko.
...Wallah. Look at me, crying at a whale remix. Don't tell my cousins.
And I'm the guy who brought a silent disco to the loudest beach in Israel. We're both kind of ridiculous.
They laugh at themselves first. The hum drops. And for a second, under the music, it has a beat.

q1_speaker.clue: The Hum has a rhythm. It pulses, like someone muttering the same thing over and over.

q2_parking.title: Friday Gridlock

obj.grisha: Talk to Grisha by the square
obj.shade: Check Grisha's shady spot by the old water tower
obj.measure: Measure Yanki's spot by the synagogue

offer: Shalom! You are the one who fixed the beach, yes? I have a spreadsheet of parking spots in the old town. Forty-one columns.
There is one spot left before Shabbat. One. And the gentleman over there has been standing in it for two hours. Standing! With a chair.
Every time one of us says 'typical', the street lights flicker. I have that in a column too. Please, talk to him.
grisha: Young man. I have been parking in this square since before it had a square. I know where the shade is. He has a spreadsheet. I have a hat.
His spot is in the sun. Mine is in the shade, by the old water tower. Go and look. Then tell him who is right.
Then the universe is broken. Go.
shade: It's true. The water tower throws perfect shade here from four o'clock to sunset. Grisha's hat would approve.
measure: Yanki's spot is exactly 4.2 metres long. His spreadsheet said 4.2. You are a little bit scared of his spreadsheet.
outro: So. Grisha's spot has the shade. Yanki's spot has the length. You each have half of the perfect spot.
I could add a column. 'Shade.' And a rota. Fridays in the shade go to whoever comes first...
...and the other one brings the tea. Fine. But I am keeping the chair.
Do you know what's funny? I made a forty-one-column spreadsheet to win one parking spot.
And I stood in the sun for two hours to defend a shady spot. We are a pair of idiots, Yanki.
They laugh. The street lights stop flickering. The hum drops again.

q2_parking.clue: The Hum got louder every time someone said 'typical'. It feeds on the little eye-rolls.

q3_tomatoes.title: Tomato Truce

obj.shiri: Talk to Shiri at the next stall
obj.sticker: Check the strange sticker on the bench
obj.back: Bring Shiri back to Orit's stall

offer: Motek, help me. My tomatoes are eight shekels a kilo. Shiri, at the next stall, sells hers at seven-ninety. Seven-ninety! Who does seven-ninety?
I said 'some people' out loud, the stall shook, and now my tomatoes are rolling all over the market.
I know, I know. Go talk to her. I'll pretend I'm not watching.
shiri: She's watching. She's always watching. Her stall plays the same song every morning and I know all the words now. Against my will.
My tomatoes rolled away too. The hum started, the crates jumped, and boom. Five tomatoes, gone.
...Huh. Okay, catch them, both piles. I'll think about it.
tomatoes: Five tomatoes, slightly bruised, extremely dramatic. You can't tell whose are whose. Nobody can.
sticker: On the bench there's a sticker of a cartoon eye, mid-roll. Under it, in tiny letters: 'THEY'RE ALL LIKE THAT.'
It hums when you touch it. Someone has been leaving these on purpose.
outro: These are your tomatoes. Or mine. I genuinely can't tell.
Because they're the same tomatoes, motek. From the same farmer. In the same moshav.
One stall. One price. Seven-ninety-five, and the chalkboard says 'Two neighbours, zero discounts.'
I argued about ten agorot for three weeks. My husband is going to laugh at me for a year.
I know the words to your song. All of them. I sing it in the shower.
The whole market laughs. The crates stop shaking. Somewhere far away, a sticker loses its hum.

q3_tomatoes.clue: The first sticker of the Heckler: a rolling eye and 'THEY'RE ALL LIKE THAT'. Someone is planting them.

q4_bbq.title: The Pharmacist's Barbecue

obj.lena: Talk to Lena by the swan lake
obj.charcoal: Collect the scattered bags of charcoal
obj.savta: Find a referee nobody can argue with

offer: Ahalan! Seven kids, one minivan the size of a bus, and the best mangal in Rishon. Ask anyone.
But the pharmacist over there says my grill is 'a public health event'. She wants to grill. On MY lawn.
When we argued, the hum knocked over my charcoal. All four bags. The kids think a swan did it.
lena: I am not angry. I am correct. That is different.
His meat is at forty degrees. It should be seventy-two. I have a thermometer. I always have a thermometer.
So... you want to grill together?
I want to win. Shesh-besh. Winner grills. But we need a referee he will not argue with. And his charcoal, obviously.
charcoal: Four bags of charcoal. One has a small handprint from one of the seven kids. Possibly two of them.
savta: A referee? For shesh-besh? Habibi, I don't referee. I play.
Bring me to them. I'll be quick. I have a bus at five.
outro: Savta Rachel beats Avi in four minutes. She beats Lena in three. She doesn't sit down for either game.
...She didn't even look at the board.
I calculated every move. She just threw the dice and laughed at me.
So now you both lost. Good. Lena holds the thermometer, Avi holds the tongs, and I eat first.
I fought a pharmacist for a lawn next to a pond full of plastic swans. Who am I?
And I brought a thermometer to a picnic. I am exactly the person I make fun of.
Everyone laughs, Savta loudest of all. The hum drops low, and the eye-rolling sticker on the picnic table peels off by itself.

q4_bbq.clue: The stickers are always exactly where someone rolled their eyes. The Heckler knows where we mutter.

q5_whatsapp.title: The WhatsApp Group

obj.alex: Talk to Alex by the mall
obj.retry: Yanki is hurt. Go back and try another tone
obj.ant1: Find the antenna that fell on the beach
obj.ant2: Find the antenna near Moshe Dayan station
obj.ant3: Find the antenna near Super-Duper Land
obj.back: Back to Yanki and Alex at the mall

c.o1: Yes. He says you flood the group with flowers every morning.
c.o2: Forget him, you know how they are, those hipsters.
c.o3: He says everyone floods it. Him too. Yesterday he sent a seven-minute voice note about sourdough.

offer: Shalom again! Remember the spreadsheet? Now I have a bigger problem: the national WhatsApp-Shmatsapp group is stuck.
Three million people in one group, all typing 'what happened to the group?' at once. The Hum is sitting on the antennas.
And the sourdough guy says it's our fault. Because of the 'good morning' pictures.
He moved to the mall. For the air conditioning. Go talk to him, I'll open a column meanwhile.
alex: Hi, you again. No, I'm not saying it's their fault. I'm saying when four hundred sunset-with-flowers pictures land every morning, something breaks.
And me? I send important things. Like voice notes about my sourdough. His name is Bezalel, by the way.
How long are the voice notes?
...Seven minutes. But it's Bezalel. Go tell Yanki to tone down the flowers.
ask: Nu? What did he say? He thinks we flood the group, right?
retry: You're back. Fine. So what did he really say?
r1: Ah. Like that. Then he can leave the group, if the flowers bother him so much.
Yanki turns and walks a few steps away. The Hum gets a little louder. Maybe there's another way to say it.
r2: ...I never thought of them like that. But now that you say it...
The Hum jumps. Yanki walks off muttering 'typical'. Oops. That is exactly how the Hum grows.
r3: yanki
Seven minutes?! I only send five!
yanki
...Wait. I send five-minute voice notes too. Oy vey.
yanki
Fine. First we bring the antennas back. The Hum knocked out three: one on the beach, one near Moshe Dayan station, one near Super-Duper Land. Open the map, they're somewhere in the area.
ant1: The first antenna lies in the sand, humming. You set it straight, and eighty 'Shabbat shalom' pictures arrive at once.
ant2: The second is stuck by the platform. You turn it, and three million people get Bezalel's voice note at the same moment.
ant3: The third is by the roller coaster. You plug it in and the group comes back to life. Just in time for an argument about parking.
outro: So: 'good morning' pictures only after nine.
And voice notes up to one minute. Bezalel too.
Bezalel can say a lot in a minute.
You know what's funny? I'm the biggest flooder in the group. I have a column for it.
And I muted the group a year ago, and still complained about it every day.
They both laugh. The national group fills with hearts. The Hum drops, but it's still there. Waiting.

q5_whatsapp.clue: At full strength the Hum jams WhatsApp. It's trying to cut us off from each other.

obj.run: Get the catering to the hall before it goes cold!

obj.ask: Now the music: talk to Moshiko the DJ

c.o3: He loves Carlebach. What about a remix? Carlebach with bass.

t.late: Savta: "By the time you get here the wedding will be a bris." Back to her, try again.

Then Savta Rachel. She's at her own home on Chispin Street. Pick her up by car and bring her to the hall gently. Don't offer her an arm when she gets in, she gets offended.
Moshiko last. If you can solve Moshiko, you can solve the Middle East.

r1: Noise? It's art, achi. Forty speakers of art.

r3: moshiko

moshiko
Go tell Avi. I'm setting up the dance floor.
delivered: You made it! And the food's still hot! Orit sent tomatoes too. Seven ninety-five.
Now Savta Rachel. She's waiting at her home on Chispin Street. Take a car and go to her.
arrived: We're here. See? Not even out of breath. You, on the other hand, braked like there's no grandmother in the car.
And what's that noise? A DJ or a power drill? Go and sort it out.
outro: Moshiko plays Carlebach with bass. Avi dances. Savta Rachel dances harder. Hodaya laughs.
I don't believe it. I'm dancing to trance. At my daughter's wedding.
And I'm crying. Like at every wedding. Don't tell anyone.
I fought with Moshiko about bass, and in the end the bass is the happiest thing here.
Someone has stuck a sticker on the cake: a rolling eye, and under it "these people...".
Those stickers again. They're all over town. Every time someone mutters "these people", the hum gets louder. That's what knocked your speakers out.
One day I'll catch whoever is sticking them. Now bring me more chicken.

q7_together.title: All Together

obj.s1: Sticker 1 of 3: by the Great Synagogue
obj.s2: Sticker 2 of 3: by the Founders' Well
obj.door: The arrow points at the Camel Cellars. Go down to the cellar
obj.ask: Talk to the person in the hoodie
obj.retry: The Heckler backed off. Find him again and try another way
obj.walk: Walk the Heckler to Founders Square
obj.wait: The Heckler is waiting for you
obj.final: Talk to Grisha in Founders' Square. Savta has gathered everyone

c.o1: You're the villain! I'll stop you!
c.o2: ...You're right. Everyone really is like that.

t.go: The Heckler walks slowly. As if he's scared of the square.
t.wait: The Heckler stopped. He won't go without you.

offer: Morning. Remember the sticker on the cake at Hodaya's wedding? Last night I saw him: someone in a hoodie, going round the old town sticking "these people..." on every post.
He ran off before I saw where. But he leaves a trail. Follow the stickers, one after another, and they'll lead you to where he hides.
Habibi, I'm a grandmother. I've seen more dangerous things in the queue at the clinic. Go.
s1: Sticker: "Those religious people...". Under it, in small print: "Those secular people...". Same handwriting.
s2: "Those street guys...", "those hipsters...". All the stickers come off the same roll.
s3: The third sticker has an arrow. It points at the Camel Cellars.
door: The stairs go down into the dark. A smell of old wine and new stickers. And there, in the corner, someone in a hoodie.
ask: Ah, you came. See? Everyone's like that. The religious, the secular, the street guys, the hipsters. I only say what everyone mutters.
Come on, you say it too. "Those people...". Feels good, doesn't it?
retry: You again. Nu, what will you say this time?
r1: He laughs and slips into another corner. You can't beat him by force. Try something else.
r2: The Hum swells and the hoodie grows a size. He backs away, pleased. That's exactly what he wanted to hear.
r3: narrator
He hesitates. Then takes off the hood.
narrator
Under it: a mirror. In the mirror, you. And Moshiko, and Alex, and Yanki, and Grisha, and Orit, and Shiri, and Avi, and Lena, and Savta.
heckler
...I'm not a villain. I'm everyone. I'm every "those people" you ever muttered.
heckler
You want me quiet? Then answer me. All of you. Together. In Founders' Square.
narrator
Savta Rachel has already posted to the WhatsApp group: "Everyone to Founders' Square. Now. Whoever doesn't come, don't come for Shabbat."
square: In Founders' Square everyone is already waiting: Yanki, Grisha, Alex, Lena, Shiri, Orit, Avi, Moshiko and Savta. Someone brought falafel. Nobody brought a chair.
The rule is simple: everyone says one good thing about someone from "these people". Out loud. In front of everyone.
outro: I'll start, because I'm the oldest. Yanki, your spreadsheet saved my Shabbat. I never told you.
Grisha, your hat is the wisest thing in town. And Alex, Bezalel is the tastiest sourdough I ever ate.
Moshiko, your playlist made a whole beach happy. Me too. Me most of all.
Avi, your daughter's wedding was the happiest one I've been to. And I only cried twice.
Lena, you were right about the thermometer. The meat really was at forty.
...And you grill the best in Rishon. But only at seventy-two.
Shiri, I love that you sing my song. Sing it louder.
Orit, your tomatoes are better. Don't tell anyone.
And me? I love all of you. Now somebody bring me a chair.
...I don't know what to do with all this. Nobody said "those people" about me.
Because "these people" is us. And we're actually all right.
With every sentence the hoodie shrinks, until only a small mirror is left on the square. In it, everyone sees themselves.
The Hum rises, rounds out, and turns into one warm chord. All over town the street lights come on together. The WhatsApp group sends one giant heart.
At dawn everyone walks to the promenade with food. Savta overtakes you with her trolley. Rishon is yours.

q7_together.clue: The villain was us. So was the answer.
